audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys[] narrative is offset from its own win[] rows. win[4] (Level 6) = 'Annie' but whys[4] said 'His R at level 6 ... flipping this phase to him'; win[5] (First item) = 'Azir' but whys[5] said 'You reclaim the edge after itemizing'. spikes[1].text and mid carried the same inversion.
audit.why: Every level-chart row renders its side next to its why. Two rows were printing 'Annie' beside a sentence explaining why Azir wins it, and vice versa.
audit.corrected: Kept the win[] rows (they match packet.levelChart) and rewrote whys[4], whys[5], spikes[1].text and mid so the prose argues for the side actually shown: level 6 is Annie's window because Emperor's Divide is 120s and he gets one attempt; first item is Azir's because a reliable ult plus soldier damage answers the only angle Tibbers gives you.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full phases[N].side disagreed with content win[]. full read Skill x6 then 'Azir'; content and packet read Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Azir/Annie. Row 6 was the worst — full said Azir, content said Annie.
audit.why: Seven rows rendering two answers each. 58.81% at 369 games supports the content/packet shape.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides flipped to match, as one group, with ratings 6/6/6/6/7/4/6 and whys rewritten to the same story.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seven fields said Azir's SOLDIERS block or shield him — whys[0] 'soldier control to reliably block your stun-engage', whys[2] 'no consistent wall or shield', spikes[0].text 'shield-block your engage', spikes[2].text 'his soldiers can shield him', early 'block your approach', wants.you[0], wants.foe[0] 'block incoming engage'.
audit.why: Sand Soldiers attack; they do not block, body-block or shield. The shield in the kit is on Shifting Sands (E), which also DASHES to a soldier — and crucially, 'If he hits an enemy champion, he ... halts his dash', so it cannot carry him through you.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real mechanics: soldiers give him a dash destination and damage, the shield is on E, and the dash halts on champion contact.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Azir ability was ever named (packet defect) and difficulty prose was generic range-war filler.
audit.why: The lane's shape is a 14-second Conquering Sands at rank 1 (the longest punish window Annie gets against any mid), a 22-second Shifting Sands as his only exit, and a 120-second Emperor's Divide that knocks her back rather than down.
audit.corrected: All five names and their cooldowns now appear across tldr, enemyWin, breakdown.* and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Emperor's Divide was described only as a wall that 'separates you from your target'. Nothing said it is a directional KNOCKBACK.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Azir summons a wall of soldiers which charge forward, knocking back and damaging enemies.' It pushes in one direction, so an engage from a flank he is not facing is far harder for him to answer — and it displaces Annie away from her own Tibbers.
audit.corrected: breakdown.carry, breakdown.late and breakdown.mid now tell the player to open from an angle the wall cannot face.
sources: brief.enemyKit R text and terrain flag

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Shifting Sands a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.corrected: Corrected to twenty-two seconds, with Conquering Sands' 14s and Emperor's Divide's 120s added to breakdown.cooldowns.

notes: Two chart problems here, not one. (1) All seven full phases[N].side disagreed with content win[] — including row 6, where full said Azir and content said Annie. (2) Inside the content layer, whys[4] and whys[5] argued for the OPPOSITE side from the win[] row they sit beside: win[4] (Level 6) said Annie while whys[4] explained why Azir wins level 6, and win[5] (First item) said Azir while whys[5] said Annie reclaims the edge. spikes[1].text and mid carried the same inversion. I kept win[] (it matches packet.levelChart) and rewrote the four prose fields to argue for the side actually displayed. Also corrected seven fields claiming Azir's SOLDIERS block or shield him — soldiers only attack; the shield is on Shifting Sands, and that dash HALTS on hitting a champion, which is the single most useful fact in the matchup and was absent. dosFull[2].d promised a fifteen-second window off a 22-second ability. Emperor's Divide is a directional knockback, which was never stated. UNRESOLVED, see questionsForUser: diff='TRICKY' and diffRating='7/10' against a 58.81% win rate at 369 games — the hardest-rated matchup in my slice is also the one Annie wins most.
